fragments: t 6.1 6.0 5.2 Django 5.2.19 release notes¶ November 3, 2026 Django 5.2.19 fixes four security issues with severity “low” and one security issue with severity “moderate” in 5.2.18. CVE-2026-108147: Potential memory exhaustion in MultiPartParser via base64-encoded file upload¶ When using django.http.multipartparser.MultiPartParser, multipart uploads with Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64 could be buffered ent

18. CVE-2026-108147: Potential memory exhaustion in MultiPartParser via base64-encoded file upload¶ When using django.http.multipartparser.MultiPartParser, multipart uploads with Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64 could be buffered entirely in memory, regardless of FILE_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE, before being passed to upload handlers, potentially consuming excessive memory. This issue has severity “low” according to the Django security policy. CVE-2026-111211: Potential log injection via unescaped geometry

cy. CVE-2026-114582: Server-side request forgery via SpatialReference string input¶ SpatialReference passed string input to GDAL, which by default resolves URLs and reads files. This behavior was not documented by Django. Other affected methods included GEOSGeometry.transform(), OGRGeometry.transform(), GDALRaster.transform(), the srs setter of OGRGeometry, and the srs and srid setters of GDALRaster. A URL or file path reaching any of these would issue an outbound request or read a file as the Django pr

ents by observing outbound requests. SpatialReference now disables network and file access when parsing string input on GDAL 3.9 and later. As a consequence, file paths and URLs are no longer accepted as SpatialReference inputs. Dictionary references using the DICT: prefix, including those prefixed with ESRI::, are rejected on all GDAL versions. Full protection requires GDAL 3.9 or later. Integer SRIDs are looked up directly in the EPSG database, so prefer them when
